request.spec: The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The people, claims and pools exports now give the as-of figures while an as-of date is set. All four tests in `bin/e2e` pass. After that run I only changed a doc comment, so I didn't run it again.

**What was wrong:** the export code was already reading as-of data, but setting the as-of date starts fresh reads. The people and claims exports didn't wait for them: clicking straight after setting the date gave a file with only the header line, because the data wasn't there yet. The pools export already re-reads before it downloads, so it didn't need a change.

**The fix (front end only):**
- `features/export/csv.ts`: a new `useSheetRead(sheet)` hook. It reports whether every read for the sheet has finished.
- `features/export/export.slot.tsx` and `features/export/exportClaims.slot.tsx`: the `export-people` and `export-claims` buttons are disabled while any of those reads is in progress. So a click right after setting or clearing the as-of date downloads once the figures for that date have loaded. I also updated each export's doc comment to say this.

Nothing changed on the server, in the stored data, in the `data-testid` values, or in the audit file.

Side effect: those two buttons are also briefly disabled whenever the sheet re-reads for any other reason, such as loading the sheet or another panel refetching.
